Laplace approximation

Source: vignettes/laplace.Rmd
laplace.Rmd

lmm_animal_laplace() and lm_phen_cov_laplace() fit the same models as the samplers by a Laplace approximation: a Gaussian at the mode on the unconstrained scale, with draws from it transformed to the reported quantities. It is not a posterior sample. There are no MCMC diagnostics, and the draw-based tools (fit_draws(), fit_loo(), breeding_values(), posterior_predictive(), imputed_data()) refuse the result. Use it to explore, then confirm with the sampler.

This vignette compares the two on the same simulated phenotypic data.

library(stanimal)
set.seed(2026)
n <- 200
X <- cbind(intercept = 1, predictor = rnorm(n))
P <- matrix(c(1, 0.4, 0.4, 1.5), 2)
Y <- X %*% rbind(c(0.5, -0.5), c(0.3, -0.2)) +
  matrix(rnorm(n * 2), n) %*% chol(P)
colnames(Y) <- c("trait1", "trait2")
approx <- lm_phen_cov_laplace(Y, X, draws = 2000, seed = 41)
#> Initial log joint probability = -14269.4 
#> Exception: lkj_corr_cholesky_lpdf: Random variable[2] is 0, but must be positive! (in '/var/folders/ph/fmqmjzln2h15bm5bstsgpng80000gn/T/RtmpBcvxLq/model-61e243024a41.stan', line 170, column 2 to column 43) 
#> Optimization terminated normally:  
#>   Convergence detected: relative gradient magnitude is below tolerance 
#> Finished in  0.1 seconds.
sampled <- lm_phen_cov(Y, X, iter = 1000, warmup = 500, chains = 2,
                       cores = 2, seed = 41, refresh = 0)
#> Running MCMC with 2 parallel chains...
#> Chain 1 finished in 0.1 seconds.
#> Chain 2 finished in 0.1 seconds.
#> 
#> Both chains finished successfully.
#> Mean chain execution time: 0.1 seconds.
#> Total execution time: 0.3 seconds.
approx
#> Laplace approximation, not a posterior sample
#>   model : lm_phen_cov_laplace 
#>   draws :2000 (seed 41)
#>   time  : 0.8 s
#> 
#> No MCMC convergence diagnostics exist for this object, and the draw-based
#> functions refuse it. Standard deviations for variances and
#> heritabilities are the least reliable entries.
#> 
#>              quantity  mean       sd
#>      P[trait1,trait1] 0.946 9.59e-02
#>      P[trait2,trait1] 0.348 8.94e-02
#>      P[trait1,trait2] 0.348 8.94e-02
#>      P[trait2,trait2] 1.619 1.56e-01
#>  corrP[trait1,trait1] 1.000 0.00e+00
#>  corrP[trait2,trait1] 0.280 6.44e-02
#>  corrP[trait1,trait2] 0.280 6.44e-02
#>  corrP[trait2,trait2] 1.000 8.91e-17
#>       sigma_P[trait1] 0.971 4.91e-02
#>       sigma_P[trait2] 1.271 6.13e-02
sampled$summary(c("P", "corrP"))[, c("variable", "mean", "sd", "rhat")]
#> # A tibble: 8 × 4
#>   variable    mean     sd  rhat
#>   <chr>      <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 P[1,1]     0.964 0.0947  1.00
#> 2 P[2,1]     0.362 0.0954  1.00
#> 3 P[1,2]     0.362 0.0954  1.00
#> 4 P[2,2]     1.66  0.174   1.00
#> 5 corrP[1,1] 1     0      NA   
#> 6 corrP[2,1] 0.286 0.0665  1.00
#> 7 corrP[1,2] 0.286 0.0665  1.00
#> 8 corrP[2,2] 1     0      NA
sampled$diagnostic_summary()
#> $num_divergent
#> [1] 0 0
#> 
#> $num_max_treedepth
#> [1] 0 0
#> 
#> $ebfmi
#> [1] 1.027234 1.100035

Agreement here does not guarantee agreement in other models. Skewed or multimodal posteriors are approximated poorly, particularly for variances and heritabilities, whose standard deviations are the least reliable entries of the approximation.
